For the universe\,$\times$\,retraining term, in the six tested universes (of 187) with a non-null shift, the standard deviation of each universe's shift over training seeds, with four degrees of freedom, is a median 1.08--1.36 times the $\sigma$ of the earlier ten-seed block, which is about 3.7 times that of the training-seed block used here.

In those universes the universe block, built at one training seed, therefore carries single-seed training noise of about the earlier seed block's size; it is part of the block as built and is not separated from the physical variation.

In two of them the noise is comparable to or larger than the shift: in \texttt{2p2h:0} the shift is \SI{0.097}{\percent} against a seed standard deviation of \SI{0.192}{\percent}, and in \texttt{MaCCQE:0} \SI{0.239}{\percent} against \SI{0.210}{\percent} (per-bin medians).
We infer that in expectation such noise adds variance to a band rather than removing it, and, from the medians, that these two bands are largely training noise.

The universe\,$\times$\,retraining values and the band-centering numbers cannot be recomputed from the saved covariance products; they were therefore not recomputed independently, and their verification is limited to the checksums of their inputs.
One systematic category provided in the input products, \texttt{NormDISCC}, is identically zero; we carry it as zero, which we have not been able to confirm is intended.
This statement and the proton-on-target statement that follows apply only to the quoted two-dimensional universe block of \S\ref{sec:uq-universes}.

No separate uncertainty is assigned to the counting of protons on target: the NuMI flux prediction carries a \SI{2}{\percent} counting term by convention, so a separate band would risk counting it twice.
Two links in that argument, that the flux universes carry the term and that the neutrino--electron constraint absorbs it, remain unverified inferences.
The twelve playlists are combined with one global exposure ratio rather than per-period ratios, and the resulting bias is not corrected.
At reconstruction level the pooled result is high, by \SI{0.18}{\percent} in total and by at most \SI{0.32}{\percent} in a marginal bin.
After unfolding, the pooled result is \SI{0.076}{\percent} above the exposure-weighted combination of the period results on the integral, the same sign as at reconstruction level.
It differs from that combination by at most \SI{0.39}{\percent} in a marginal bin (the highest $\pPar$ bin) and by at most \SI{0.33}{\percent} in $\pT$.
In single cells the combination differs from the pooled result by \SIrange{-1.83}{3.78}{\percent}, each with $|z|$ at most 0.31.
The block's interpretation is limited by the small number of period groups, by possible shrinkage from the regularization, and by the statistical and training noise it retains.

Assigning one would require a suite of injection shapes and amplitudes specified before the tests are run.
Calibration to a single Gaussian bump would leave that requirement unmet.
The follow-up assessment~\cite{TwoDFollowup2026} distinguishes a proposed split-sample width check from repeated-sampling coverage.
With the MC sample, binning maps and background subtraction held fixed, such a check could establish only the precision conditional on them, at its tested exposure.
Nonlinear unfolding does not guarantee a simple scaling from half to full exposure.
Nor can the check supply the variation across independent MC populations.
With the current inputs, validated total uncertainties for all 205 bins, the integral and the projections therefore cannot be obtained.

They would require independent populations or a validated generative law, a continuous nuisance generator for tests of total intervals, and an untouched generator-truth domain for bias checks (\S\ref{sec:uq-2d-scope}).
This is a limit of the available inputs, not a general impossibility result for 2D unfolding.

column7: The test concerns the statistical band alone and changes no central value or quoted uncertainty.
It tests the LightGBM statistical estimator at the band's training seed (seed~1), while the quoted central value uses seed~42.
Systematic, total and five-dimensional coverage are outside this test's scope.
Its simulation-side scatter reuses the resampling that built the band.
Only the data-side fluctuation is tested by an independent mechanism.
Because $T$ equals the prior, the test cannot detect regularization bias toward the prior.
The test resolves a per-cell deficit in content of about \lrval{cov2d-res-cell}, and about \lrval{cov2d-res-joint} jointly; smaller deficits can pass.
It is one-sided: over-coverage is reported, not failed.

The pseudo-experiments depart from the null's law in known ways: the flux and pair-band draws are not centered, clipping truncates the shifts by setting a negative composite weight to zero, separately on the reconstructed side and on the truth side, and three terms are in the remade covariance and are not drawn in the pseudo-experiments (the training-seed block, \S\ref{sec:uq-ml}, $C_{\mathrm{model}}$ and the simulation-statistics part of the statistical term).
Their effect on the flag rate was not measured.
The false-flag rates are those of a null in which the remade covariance is exact.

That covariance is itself estimated from finite ensembles, and the estimation can make $\chi^{2}$ and each cell's standardized difference larger than this null allows, most along the covariance's smallest-eigenvalue directions, whose estimates are least precise.
No correction for this is made, and the verdict stands as graded under this null.
\fvval{f1-tune-g18} shares its 2p2h model family with one of the model term's generators.
The run-period block was not drawn.
The result concerns the procedure's covariance at those two tunes, not the reported intervals at the data, where the quoted covariance is made.
It is not a coverage rate, says nothing about truths unlike these two or about $C_{\mathrm{PL}}$ or $C_{\mathrm{model}}$, and gives no cause for the joint under-coverage or for any flag.
A held-out tune moves the truth, not the sample, so this is not the re-test on held-out simulation of \S\ref{sec:coverage}.
